q6.answer: The Order service is the coordinator. It starts each step by calling other services over HTTP or reacting to their events. The record of progress is the order's status in Order's own database (PENDING, RESERVED, PAID, CONFIRMED and so on). Each other service also keeps its own record, such as the payment row and the reservation.

q7.answer: The provider calls a webhook endpoint on the Payment service. Payment records the outcome, then publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event on the broker, written to its own database first and sent by a relay. Order consumes that event and finishes the order.

q8.answer: Payment inserts the provider's event id into processed_events, which has a unique constraint. A repeat returns 200 and does nothing. Downstream, every consumer also acts on an event only when its record is in the status that event expects, for example Order handles PaymentSucceeded only while RESERVED, and otherwise ignores it.

q9.answer: Payment sets DECLINED and publishes PaymentDeclined. Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and calls Inventory's release(order id) once. If that call fails, the Inventory timer that runs every minute expires the hold and puts the stock back on sale.

q10.answer: Order asks Inventory to claim the stock, and Inventory decides in one local transaction. If the hold is intact it marks the stock SOLD. If the hold lapsed but all stock is still free it re-takes every line and sells it. If any line was sold to someone else it refuses with 409 and changes nothing, so Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and requests a full refund.

q11.answer: The refund is a stored row in Payment, so it is not an in-memory retry. On failure the status becomes REFUND_RETRYING and Payment retries with backoff using the same idempotency key (refund-<order id>). After N failed tries it becomes REFUND_NEEDS_ATTENTION, ops are alerted, and retries continue. The value of N was left open.

q12.answer: After Order sets CONFIRMED it publishes an OrderConfirmed event. The Cart service consumes it and empties the cart, ignoring a repeated event for the same order. The cart is not cleared at any other point.
